title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcement + fix circuit-breaker misfires; add regional failover load-shedding
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Hotfix: tighten SLO enforcement thresholds, fix circuit-breaker misfires causing premature tripping, add emergency load-shedding and regional failover policy; no API changes.
body: Summary: This hotfix tightens SLO enforcement and fixes a bug where the circuit-breaker state machine could mis-evaluate transient KV-cache errors and trigger unnecessary global tripping. In addition to the bug fix, the PR introduces an emergency load-shedding policy and regional failover wiring so that when a region crosses its high-error SLO for >30s we failover traffic to backup region(s) and shed low-priority requests first. Motivation: During the 2026-02-24 incident we saw a cascade where circuit-breakers tripped globally due to localized KV cache consistency errors. This caused multi-region failovers to engage and increased tail latency for high-priority customers. The goal here is to: (1) fix the misfire bug, (2) make SLO enforcement stricter in the controller (fewer false positives), (3) add targeted load-shedding ordered by request priority, and (4) add an automated regional failover policy that only triggers after sustained SLO violations. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce misfire locally and add unit tests - [x] Fix state machine race in circuit_breaker.rs - [x] Add scoped load-shedding strategy and prioritization - [x] Add regional failover orchestration + graceful draining - [x] Add integration tests in perf-canary harness - [x] Add telemetry (SLO breach reasons, shed_count by priority, failover events) - [x] Canary rollout to 5% of traffic and monitor for 2h - [x] Postmortem link: SUP-1182 and ENG-4321 Changes (high level): - src/runtime/circuit_breaker.rs: fix race where transient cache errors could be treated as hard failures; add hysteresis and per-region counters instead of global counters. - src/runtime/load_shed.rs: new file implementing priority-ordered shedding and an async token bucket for soft-degrades. - src/runtime/failover/orchestrator.rs: add regional failover policy, max-failover-per-hour guard, and drain handlers. - infra/k8s/redwood-controller-deploy.yaml: rollout config to enable canary flag (feature.flag.slo_2026_hotfix). - observability/metrics/slo_labels.md: document new metrics and labels. - docs/operational/playbooks/regional-failover.md: initial ops runbook for on-call. Commits summary: - f2c9d8a: fix(cb): prevent transient cache errors tripping global breaker - 8f3b2c1: feat(load-shed): implement priority-based shedding + tests - a44d1e7: feat(failover): orchestrator and drain handlers + telemetry - b12f0ef: infra: add canary rollout flag and k8s tweak - 4e7a3b2: docs: playbook and metrics docs Review conversation: - Marcus Lee (review): "Can you add a unit test that simulates an interleaved cache timeout + recovery? I want to see the hysteresis behavior in CI." Asha: "Added a deterministic integration test that simulates the timeout/recovery sequence and asserts no global trip within the hysteresis window (see tests/cb_hysteresis_test.rs)." - Evelyn Zhou (review): "How does this interact with the existing model-variant fallback? Will failover cause double-fallbacks?" Asha: "Failover is region->region routing; we explicitly bypass model-variant fallback during failover to avoid layered fallbacks. The orchestrator marks requests as 'failover' and the router treats that as a single-level failover target." - Priya Nair (approve): "Telemetry looks sufficient; watch slo.breach_reason tag cardinality in canary." CI and rollout: - Initial CI run failed lint on a naming nit and one flaky test in perf-canary; both were fixed and CI passed on rerun. - Integration: perf-canary run (canary harness) shows expected reduction in global breaker trips under injected KV flakiness and stable tail latency for high-priority requests. - Canary: rolled out to 5% for 2 hours, monitored key SLOs and telemetry; no customer-impacting regressions observed. Merge: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI. Post-merge action items: - Backfill rollout config to Dedicated clusters (ENG-4388). - Schedule 24h observation window and follow-up on telemetry cardinality (assigned to Priya). - Ship a short ops note to on-call and SRE slack channel. Linked work: SUP-1182 (incident), ENG-4321 (follow-up), ENG-4388 (dedicated rollout).
